newsitem.title: USA: AAA says U.S. self-serve gasoline down 5 cts/gal.
newsitem.headline: AAA says U.S. self-serve gasoline down 5 cts/gal.

text.p: U.S. motorists can expect a break on gasoline prices this Fourth of July, according to the American Automobile Association.
The average price of self-serve regular unleaded gasoline in the U.S. is about 1.25 cents a gallon, 5.3 cents below the year-ago level, the AAA reported Tuesday.

The western part of the U.S. showed the highest price, with regular gasoline averaging $1.355 a gallon, though that figures was a hefty 9.5 cents below the 1996 figure. The Southeast had the cheapest gasoline at 1.17 cents a gallon, 4.6 cents below the year-ago mark.

Self-serve gasoline in New England averaged $1.267, down 6.1 cents a gallon from last year, while the Mid-Atlantic sat at $1.233, down 8.7 cents, and the Midwest sat at $1.244, down 1.4 cents. Southwest gasoline averaged $1.230 a gallon, down 5.7 cents and the Great Lakes area prices averaged $1.228, down 4.7 cents.
AAA is a not-for-profit federation of clubs with more than 39 million members in the U.S. and Canada.
